newsitem.title: USA: Clarcor sees UAS Q2 weaker than year-ago.
newsitem.headline: Clarcor sees UAS Q2 weaker than year-ago.

text.p: Clarcor Inc said it expects its recently acquired United Air Specialists unit to report a second quarter weaker than 1996's second quarter, which was unusually strong.

"Despite a loss of a significant customer in Great Britain, we still expect UAS to have a good year as sales of its air quality products are up substantially so far this year from 1996. As we realize synergies between UAS and Airguard Industries, we expect an even better 1998 for both companies," said the filters maker.

Clarcor said it is still experiencing losses at its Hastings Filters unit. "These losses are larger than we had expected and are primarily related to start-up costs at the expanded Yankton, S.D., plant. We have placed additional manufacturing resources in the plant and we expect productivity improvements in the near future," Clarcor said.
"It now appears that Hastings will not be profitable for fiscal 1997, but we expect that it will become profitable by the end of the year," the company said.
The company said it expects its J.L. Clark unit to show a strong single-digit increase in both sales and operating profit for 1997.

Clarcor reported first quarter 1997 net sales grew 7.3 percent and operating profit before merger-related costs increased 5.9 percent. Net earnings fell by 19.6 percent after the impact of unusual items, the company said.

"We are very disappointed by the performance of Hastings Filters. We are working very hard to fix the problems at Hastings and expect to do so this year. We also expect our other filtration companies and J.L. Clark to continue to have a superior year. Excluding the first quarter's unusual items, we believe that 1997 will be another record year of sales and net earnings for Clarcor," said chief executive Larry Gloyd.
